_comment: HAND-MAINTAINED INPUT to p-stream-surface-union. The probe ASSERTS against this file and never writes it: a probe that generates its own expectation and then checks it asserts nothing (PROJECT_MAP Principle 9, Q3). Add a pair only after seeing it in a real stream, and classify it deliberately — `render | ignore | escalate` is a product decision about what a non-coder is shown, not a fact the engine can tell you.
_schema: A pair entry carries EXACTLY ONE of `class` or `when`. `class` is an unconditional decision. `when` is a value-conditional one: read `path` (dot-separated, from the event root), look the value up in `values`, and fall back to `unknown` if it is not there. `unknown` MUST be `escalate` — a rule that discriminates by value is a statement that the values matter, so an unrecognised one has to reach a human. schemaVersion 1 had `class` only, which is why two of its three `escalate` entries were wrong: `rate_limit_event` fires on EVERY healthy session (measured `rate_limit_info.status = "allowed"`), and a renderer obeying that file literally would escalate every phase forever. Alarm fatigue then kills the one escalation that matters, which is the rate-limit pause the class was written for.
defaultForUnknownWhy: The runtime rule for a pair that is in NO list. This file is a sample of one flag configuration, never the closed set (see `scope`), so incompleteness is not a risk to be managed but a certainty to be survived. A renderer that drops what it does not recognise goes silent in front of a non-coder, which REVIEW-02 names as the worst available outcome; one that escalates is merely noisy, and the noise is a bug report.
_findings: Two entries here were NOT in the REVIEW-02 §13 seed and were found by this probe's first live run: the pair `system/status`, and content-bearing thinking blocks (`event.content_block.type=thinking`, `event.delta.type=thinking_delta`, `event.delta.type=signature_delta`). The second answers the open half of REVIEW-02 A6 as a side effect: raw reasoning text DOES reach `-p` stream-json, on haiku, unrewritten by the MessageDisplay hook.
scope: A SAMPLE OF ONE FLAG CONFIGURATION **ON ONE MODEL**, NOT THE CLOSED SET. Every pair below was observed in a real stream, but the union of one configuration is not the union of all of them. Configurations NOT represented here: sessions that use tools, subagents (--forward-subagent-text), MCP servers, --json-schema, a non-zero-exit result, an interrupted session, or a rate-limited one. `result/success` is present and the other `result/*` subtypes are deliberately ABSENT because none has been observed by this suite — so a run that ends in an error result WILL fail this probe, which is the intended behaviour: it forces the new subtype to be classified by a human before the cockpit meets it.
_modelDependence: THE MODEL CHANGES THE UNION, measured 2026-07-31. Identical flags on `--model sonnet --effort high` produced NO thinking surface at all — no `content_block.type=thinking`, no `thinking_delta`, no `signature_delta`, and no `system/thinking_tokens` — where `--model haiku` produces all four. The whole conformance suite runs on haiku, so this file is haiku's universe. A cockpit validated here and run on another model is validated against a different stream. Effort level, by contrast, does NOT change the surface: low/medium/high/xhigh/max and no-flag all produced the same three thinking types on haiku, varying only in volume (157-299 chars).
seededFrom: docs/research/REVIEW-02-runtime-gaps.md §13 — the eight pairs measured in one short session
p-stream-json-roundtrip (baseline: pass) — evidences that `user` and `stream_event` appear under --replay-user-messages + --include-partial-messages
S1 night cycle 1, this probe's own first live run under the configuration recorded in `observedUnder`

flags: + the ADR-008 isolation pair added by the harness
observedUnder.model: haiku (the suite's live default — the wire format is under test, not reasoning)

classes.render: The cockpit turns this into user-facing plain language.
classes.ignore: Deliberately not shown to the user. Consumed by the orchestrator, or dropped.
classes.escalate: Must interrupt the normal flow — the user has to be told, or a gate has to act.

requiredPairsWhy: Without a pinned minimum this probe passes on an empty or truncated stream: it would observe nothing, find no unclassified pair, and report green having learned nothing. Every entry here is structurally guaranteed by the flag set in `observedUnder` and is already evidenced green by p-stream-json-roundtrip.

system/init.why: Consumed by the ADR-008 init-receipt gate as a pre-flight assertion before any work. Never rendered; it is engineer-facing configuration.

system/hook_started.why: Hook lifecycle. Internal to the behaviour pack; a non-coder has no model of what a hook is.

system/thinking_tokens.why: Counters only (estimated_tokens, estimated_tokens_delta) and no text, measured REVIEW-02 §13. May drive a progress indicator later; it is not a render surface.

assistant.why: The completed assistant message. This is the text the MessageDisplay rewrite acts on (ADR-008) and the primary user-facing surface.

user.why: Replay of the message the orchestrator itself sent (--replay-user-messages). Rendering it would echo the user's own words back at them as if the engine had said them.

stream_event.why: Token-level deltas that drive the live activity feed. See `innerPairs` — the outer envelope is not enough to render from.

rate_limit_event.why: Night Shift sleeps to resetsAt (ADR-007), and a paused run that looks identical to a working one is the worst outcome in front of a non-coder — so the PAUSE must reach the surface. The event itself does not mean a pause: it is emitted on every healthy session. `allowed` (measured 2026-07-31 morning, alongside resetsAt, rateLimitType: five_hour, overageStatus, overageDisabledReason, isUsingOverage) is routine and ignored. `allowed_warning` was found the same evening BY THE ADAPTER ESCALATING IT — the fail-closed default doing its job on a value nobody had modelled — carrying `rateLimitType: "seven_day"` and a new `utilization: 0.51` field. It is classified `render`, not `escalate`: the user should be told they are half way through a weekly allowance, and interrupting them for it would be the alarm fatigue this schema exists to prevent, while hiding it would make work stopping later a surprise. `rejected` and anything else still escalate by falling through.

system/status.why: NOT IN THE REVIEW-02 §13 SEED — first observed by this probe in S1 night cycle 1, and it rides with --include-partial-messages (absent from a run without it, measured 2026-07-31). Keys are {type, subtype, session_id, uuid, status}. `status = "requesting"` is measured and is a request-progress signal, not a session-level alarm, so it is `ignore` on the same reasoning as system/thinking_tokens: it may drive a spinner, it is not a render surface. It was classified `escalate` unconditionally as a fail-closed placeholder while its values were unmeasured; that placeholder was correct then and would be alarm noise now. The rest of the value set is STILL unenumerated, which is exactly what `unknown: escalate` is for.

result/success.why: Terminal event. Carries usage/cost and closes the phase; the cockpit shows completion from this, never from the model claiming it finished.

innerPairs._comment: Inside a `stream_event` envelope. Asserted with the same no-unclassified-pair rule as `pairs`, but only the two entries in `requiredInnerPairs` are required to appear — the rest are absence-tolerant because which content blocks a session produces depends on what it was asked to do. A NEW inner type is still a FAIL, which is the drift this section exists to catch. REVIEW-02 A6 (thinking content blocks) is the open half and is a separate probe.

event.type=content_block_start.why: Opens a renderable block; the block's own type decides how.

event.type=content_block_delta.why: The token stream itself — this is the live feed.

event.type=message_delta.why: Carries stop_reason and usage deltas, not text. The orchestrator reads it; the user does not.

event.delta.type=text_delta.why: Assistant text, one chunk at a time.

event.content_block.type=thinking.why: RAW CHAIN-OF-THOUGHT, ON THE WIRE. Keys {type, thinking, signature}. Measured S1 night cycle 1 on `--model haiku` with no reasoning flag beyond --include-partial-messages, so this is the DEFAULT shape, not an opt-in one. The MessageDisplay rewrite fires on assistant text and NOT on thinking (ADR-008), so this text arrives unrewritten — the most engineer-facing text the engine produces. It must be in the renderer's ignore set BY NAME. A whitelist that ignores it by omission fails open the moment the renderer is rewritten.

event.delta.type=thinking_delta.why: Streaming chunks of the above. Keys {type, thinking, estimated_tokens}. Same rule, same reason: ignored by name, never by omission.

event.delta.type=signature_delta.why: Cryptographic signature over a thinking block. Keys {type, signature}. No user-facing meaning at all; carried so a thinking block can be replayed to the API intact.

requiredInnerPairsWhy: A session that emits a `stream_event` envelope but no text delta inside it has a feed with no content. These two are the minimum that makes --include-partial-messages worth passing at all.
